description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern feast, featuring succulent slow-roasted lamb served atop aromatic spiced rice. This impressive dish is traditionally prepared for special occasions, offering a symphony of tender meat, fragrant spices, and crunchy nuts. It is a true centerpiece that promises a memorable culinary experience for all your guests.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb Marinade
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, seven-spice blend, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Mix well to form a paste. Pat the lamb dry and rub the marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into any crevices. Place the lamb in a large roasting pan, add the quartered onion, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick. Pour 2 cups of water or broth into the pan. Cover tightly with foil and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Place the covered roasting pan in the preheated oven and slow roast for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls apart. For the last 30 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown slightly. Once cooked, carefully remove the lamb from the pan and let it rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for at least 15-20 minutes before shredding or slicing. Reserve the pan juices.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice Base
instructions.text: While the lamb is roasting, prepare the rice. Rinse the basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak it in warm water for 20-30 minutes, then drain well. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat vegetable oil or ghee over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. If using, add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat.

instructions.title: Cook the Spiced Rice
instructions.text: Add the seven-spice blend, cinnamon, crushed cardamom pods, salt, and black pepper to the pot with the onion and meat. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the drained basmati rice and stir gently to coat the grains with the spices. Pour in the 4 cups of water or lamb broth (you can use some of the reserved lamb pan juices, strained, if desired). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.

instructions.title: Finish the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, gently fold in the frozen peas and diced carrots. Cover again and let it steam off the heat for another 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the vegetables to warm through. Fluff the rice gently with a fork.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: To serve, spread a generous layer of the spiced Ouzi rice onto a large serving platter. Arrange the shredded or sliced slow-roasted lamb over the rice. Drizzle some of the strained lamb pan juices over the meat and rice for extra flavor. Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and freshly chopped parsley. Serve hot with a side of yogurt, a fresh salad, or a cucumber and mint raita.

tips: For extra depth of flavor, marinate the lamb overnight. This allows the spices to penetrate deeply into the meat, resulting in a more aromatic and tender roast.
If you dont have a seven-spice blend, you can create your own by mixing equal parts ground allspice, black pepper, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, ginger, and cardamom. Adjust to your taste.
To ensure the lamb is incredibly tender, maintain a low and slow oven temperature throughout the roasting process. The meat should easily pull apart with a fork when done.
Serve Lamb Ouzi with a cooling side like a simple yogurt sauce, a cucumber and mint salad, or a fresh green salad to balance the richness of the dish.
Store leftover lamb and rice separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of broth to the rice if it seems dry.
article:
Unveiling the majestic centerpiece of Middle Eastern feasting, Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is more than just a meal; it's a celebration, a culinary spectacle that embodies warmth, hospitality, and an unforgettable symphony of flavors. This traditional dish, often reserved for special occasions, family gatherings, and festive holidays, showcases succulent, fall-off-the-bone lamb, slow-roasted to perfection, served atop a fragrant bed of spiced rice, garnished with toasted nuts and tender peas. Preparing a true Lamb Ouzi Recipe is a labor of love, but the reward is an experience that transcends the ordinary, transporting your senses to the heart of the Levant.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled "Ozzi" or "Ozi," is a distinguished dish with roots deeply embedded in the culinary traditions of the Middle East, particularly in countries like Jordan, Palestine, Syria, and Lebanon. At its core, Ouzi represents abundance and generosity. While variations exist, the quintessential Ouzi features a large cut of lamb – typically a whole lamb shoulder, leg, or even a small whole lamb – that has been marinated and then slow-roasted until incredibly tender. The star meat is then presented magnificently, often nestled on or served alongside a rich, aromatic rice pilaf that has been cooked with an array of warming spices such as cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and nutmeg. The rice is usually studded with green peas and toasted nuts like pine nuts and slivered almonds, adding texture and depth to every bite. Unlike a simple roasted lamb, Ouzi is a complete, elaborate platter designed to be shared, making it the ultimate expression of Middle Eastern hospitality and a truly impressive Lamb Ouzi Recipe.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Crafting an authentic Lamb Ouzi Recipe requires a selection of quality ingredients that contribute to its rich, complex flavor profile. Here’s what you’ll need to embark on this culinary journey:

*   **For the Lamb:**
    *   1 whole lamb shoulder or leg (bone-in, 5-7 lbs/2.3-3.2 kg) – bone-in adds immense flavor and moisture.
    *   Olive oil
    *   **Spice Rub:**
        *   2 tbsp Baharat spice blend (a staple Middle Eastern mix, or make your own with paprika, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, nutmeg, cardamom, black pepper)
        *   1 tbsp ground cinnamon
        *   1 tsp ground cardamom
        *   1 tsp ground cloves
        *   1 tsp ground ginger
        *   1 tsp black pepper
        *   Salt to taste (generous amount)
        *   6-8 cloves garlic, minced
        *   1 onion, roughly chopped
        *   Juice of 1 lemon

*   **For the Spiced Rice:**
    *   3 cups Basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
    *   3 tbsp olive oil or ghee
    *   1 large onion, finely chopped
    *   4 cloves garlic, minced
    *   1 tbsp Baharat spice blend
    *   1 tsp ground cinnamon
    *   1/2 tsp ground cardamom
    *   1/4 tsp ground cloves
    *   1/2 cup frozen green peas
    *   6 cups hot lamb or chicken broth (or water)
    *   Salt to taste

*   **For Garnish:**
    *   1/2 cup pine nuts
    *   1/2 cup slivered almonds
    *   2 tbsp olive oil or butter (for toasting nuts)
    *   Fresh parsley, chopped (for serving)

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Lamb Ouzi

This detailed Lamb Ouzi Recipe will guide you through creating a masterpiece that will impress any guest.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:**
    *   Pat the lamb shoulder or leg dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make several deep incisions all over the lamb.
    *   In a small bowl, combine all the lamb spice rub ingredients (Baharat, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, ginger, black pepper, salt, minced garlic, chopped onion, lemon juice, and olive oil) to form a thick paste.
    *   Generously rub the spice paste all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the incisions. For best results, cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate deeply.
    *   Before roasting, bring the lamb to room temperature for about 1-2 hours.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C).
    *   Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. You can add a cup of water or broth to the bottom of the pan to help keep the lamb moist.
    *   Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil.
    *   Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb cut. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up slightly.
    *   Once done, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a carving board, tent it loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This is crucial for juicy, tender meat. Reserve any pan juices.

3.  **Prepare the Spiced Rice:**
    *   While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or ghee over medium heat.
    *   Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
    *   Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
    *   Stir in the Baharat, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the spices are aromatic.
    *   Add the rinsed Basmati rice to the pot and stir well to coat every grain with the spiced oil. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
    *   Pour in the hot broth (and any reserved lamb pan juices for extra flavor), add salt to taste, and bring to a boil.
    *   Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, stir in the frozen green peas, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
    *   Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for another 10 minutes. Then, fluff the rice gently with a fork.

4.  **Toast the Nuts:**
    *   In a small skillet, heat olive oil or butter over medium-low heat. Add the pine nuts and slivered almonds.
    *   Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and fragrant. Be careful not to burn them, as they can go from toasted to burnt very quickly. Remove from heat immediately.

## Tips for the Perfect Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving the ultimate Lamb Ouzi Recipe requires a few insider tricks:

*   **Quality Lamb is Key:** Always opt for a good quality, bone-in cut of lamb. The bone adds incredible flavor and helps keep the meat moist during the long roasting process.
*   **Marination Time:** Don't rush the marination. Allowing the lamb to marinate overnight or for at least 8 hours makes a significant difference in the depth of flavor.
*   **Low and Slow:** Patience is a virtue when slow roasting. A lower temperature over a longer period ensures the lamb becomes incredibly tender and succulent, literally falling off the bone.
*   **Resting the Lamb:** This step is non-negotiable! Resting allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, resulting in a more tender and flavorful lamb.
*   **Don't Overcook the Rice:** Basmati rice cooks relatively quickly. Follow the instructions carefully to avoid mushy rice. Fluffing it gently with a fork after resting helps separate the grains.
*   **Toasting Nuts:** Toasting the pine nuts and almonds enhances their flavor and adds a delightful crunch. Watch them closely, as they can burn quickly.

## Serving Suggestions for Middle Eastern Lamb Ouzi

The presentation of a Lamb Ouzi Recipe is as important as its taste. This dish is designed to be a showstopper!

Traditionally, the slow-roasted lamb is placed whole on a large, ornate platter, surrounded by the fragrant spiced rice. Garnish generously with the toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley.

Accompaniments that perfectly complement the richness of the Ouzi include:

*   **Yogurt Sauce (Laban):** A simple yogurt sauce, perhaps flavored with garlic and mint, provides a refreshing contrast.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Crisp, tangy salads like Fattoush (bread salad) or Tabbouleh (parsley and bulgur salad) cut through the richness.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles add a briny, acidic counterpoint.
*   **Warm Pita Bread:** Perfect for scooping up the lamb and rice.
*   **Fresh Vegetables:** Sliced cucumbers and tomatoes can offer a light, refreshing element.

## Variations and Substitutions for Ouzi

While the classic Lamb Ouzi Recipe is magnificent, there are several ways to adapt it to personal preferences or available ingredients:

*   **Meat Alternatives:** While lamb is traditional, you could use goat meat for a similar rich flavor. For a slightly different take, some recipes use large pieces of chicken, though the cooking time would be significantly reduced.
*   **Rice Variations:** While Basmati is preferred for its long grains and aroma, you could experiment with other long-grain rice varieties. Some regional Ouzi versions might incorporate small pasta (like orzo or vermicelli) sautéed with the rice.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Feel free to adjust the spice levels to your liking. If you don't have Baharat, a mix of equal parts cumin, coriander, paprika, and a pinch of cinnamon and cardamom can be a good substitute. Some prefer a touch more turmeric for color and earthy notes.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Beyond peas, you can add finely diced carrots, chickpeas, or even roasted eggplant pieces to the rice for extra texture and flavor.
*   **Stuffed Ouzi:** In some more elaborate preparations, the spiced rice mixture is actually stuffed *inside* a deboned lamb shoulder or even a whole small lamb before roasting, creating an even more integrated flavor profile and a truly grand presentation. This takes the Lamb Ouzi Recipe to another level of culinary artistry.

Embarking on the journey to create a Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is a rewarding culinary adventure. It's a dish that speaks volumes of tradition, celebration, and the joy of sharing good food. This comprehensive Lamb Ouzi Recipe will empower you to bring a taste of authentic Middle Eastern grandeur to your own table, creating memories that will linger long after the last succulent bite.
